edition.intro: This week's edit is all about wearing more of what you already own, with a few smart, versatile pieces for fall.

items.snippet: Read this if you want to start getting your closet ready for 2027 now.
items.headline: How to Clean Out Your Closet: What to Keep, Toss, and Replace
items.summary: Professional organizers say a good cleanout is about thoughtful choices, not getting rid of as much as possible. They suggest editing before you organize, tackling one category at a time, and being honest about what you actually wear. Everyday basics are worth replacing when they wear out, while coats and blazers can often be repaired or tailored.
items.tip: Pick one category, like sweaters or shoes, and edit just that this week.

items.title: Ask Earl With Laurel Pantin: How to Style Leopard as a Neutral
items.snippet: In her monthly column, Ask Earl, writer, editor, mom, and entrepreneur, Laurel Pantin answers your latest style questions.
items.headline: How to Style Leopard Print as a Neutral
items.summary: Laurel Pantin argues that animal print works like a neutral because its colors are so easy to pair with others. Her approach is to keep it nearly tonal, add casual pieces like sweatshirts or denim, and bring in something slightly quirky so the outfit feels personal rather than costume-like. Her advice to a tired shopper is to mix well-worn favorites with more polished pieces.
items.tip: Pair a leopard piece with your favorite jeans or a sweatshirt to dial down the drama.

items.title: Brown Midiskirts That'll Go With Every Shoe in Your Closet This Fall
items.snippet: It's rare to find a piece that works with heels, boots, and sneakers.
items.headline: Brown Midiskirts Are This Fall's Easy Shoe-Friendly Staple
items.summary: Brown midiskirts are showing up everywhere this season, working either as a grounding base for brighter colors or as the star of an all-brown look. They go with heels, loafers, ballet flats, and even sneakers. Details like leather, ruffles, or animal print can freshen up the style.
items.tip: Try a brown skirt with a black top and the flats or loafers you already own.

items.title: The Art of the Evening Sweater: 5 Silhouettes to Wear All Winter Long
items.snippet: These sumptuous knits are anything but frumpy.
items.headline: Five Evening Sweater Styles to Wear All Winter
items.summary: Knitwear can feel dressy enough for a night out if it has one sultry detail, such as a wrap waist, a draped neckline, or an open back. The idea is to stay warm while still looking polished and a little daring. Sleeveless knits also layer neatly under a leather jacket.
items.tip: Look for a sweater with just one standout detail, like a wrap front or a low neckline, and wear it with jeans.

items.title: The Best Knee-Length Skirts Worth Adding to Your Closet
items.snippet: From polished pencils to effortless denim, these are the skirts to shop now.
items.headline: Why the Knee-Length Skirt Never Goes Out of Style
items.summary: The knee-length skirt endures because its hemline is flattering on many body types and works with flats, boots, and heels. The fabric sets the mood, from structured wool to silky satin to relaxed denim. This roundup mixes splurge-worthy classics with more affordable options.
items.tip: Try a knee-length skirt in a fabric you don't usually wear to see how it shifts your style.

items.title: No Need To Guess—6 Fall Shoe Trends Fashion People Are Wearing Right Now
items.snippet: From animal print to penny loafers.
items.headline: Six Fall Shoe Trends Fashion People Are Wearing Now
items.summary: This season's shoe trends include animal print, jewel tones, tall boots with sleeker toes, and ballet pumps with a small heel. Sleek penny loafers are replacing chunky soles, and elegant slipper-style shoes are gaining ground. Each trend offers a simple way to update outfits you already have.
items.tip: If you buy one pair, choose a sleek loafer or a small-heeled ballet pump that works with several outfits.

items.title: 11 Best Men's Dress Shirts 2026, According to GQ Editors
items.snippet: Forget haggling with HR or securing a competing offer—just button up one of these.
items.headline: The Best Men's Dress Shirts, According to GQ
items.summary: GQ's editors say a well-chosen dress shirt is useful far beyond formal events, since the right fit, fabric, and details let it work in casual settings too. Their top picks include a classic Oxford from J.Crew, a surprisingly solid budget option from Uniqlo, and a splurge from Todd Snyder. A good collar and a slim but not skin-tight fit matter most.
items.tip: Try wearing a crisp dress shirt untucked over a tee or with jeans for an easy upgrade.

practice: Start by shopping your closet: pull out just one category, like skirts or sweaters, and keep only what fits and feels like you. Try your most worn-in favorites, such as old jeans or a tee, with something more polished, and let a leopard or brown piece work as your neutral. Take anything that needs mending or tailoring, like a coat or blazer, to a repair shop before deciding to replace it.

If you do buy something, keep it to one or two versatile pieces: a brown or knee-length skirt, a sleek loafer or low-heeled pump, or a knit with one interesting neckline. Those pieces should work with the clothes you already own, such as denim, a plain tee, or a leather jacket. For men, a well-fitting dress shirt can do the same job, dressing up jeans or smartening a tee.
